note: Where each count comes from, when it moves, what resets it, and what it does when it runs out of bits. A counter whose event is not written down is a number nobody can argue with.

reset.rule: every counter clears on rst_n and on nothing else
reset.epoch: a launch does NOT clear them. The host reads them before and after and subtracts, which is what makes a region of interest a region rather than a whole run. R2's epoch change restarts the device process, so it clears them the same way a reset does.
reset.why: clearing on launch would make a counter unreadable for any window that contains a launch, and the multi-batch grids of R2-09 are exactly that

overflow.rule: wraps. At one event per cycle a 64-bit counter needs 5.8e11 seconds to wrap, so the defined behaviour is stated rather than guarded against in hardware.
overflow.narrow: a counter narrower than 64 bits must say so here and must saturate rather than wrap, because a wrap in a narrow counter is reachable and a saturated one is at least ordered

perf_cycles.event: one per cycle while any role context is running

perf_issued.event: one per instruction that leaves the issue stage

stall_exclusive.note: Every blocked cycle is charged to exactly one of these, by the fixed priority below. Their sum equals perf_stall_total over any window. This is the group COUNT-02 means by 主stall互斥计数.

perf_stall_total.event: one per cycle where stall_front is true and something is running

perf_x_fpu.event: the FP reduction unit is busy

perf_x_arrive.event: a barrier arrive cannot be taken

perf_x_rsv.event: the writeback slot this instruction needs is reserved

perf_x_wb.event: a completion stole the writeback port

stall_overlapping.note: The same cycles counted per cause, WITHOUT exclusivity: a cycle blocked by both a hazard and the LSU appears in both. Listed separately because 'how many cycles did the LSU contribute to' is a real question with a different answer, and because adding these up does not give a time. COUNT-02: 重叠计数另列，不重复累计总体时间.

n_grant.event: one per read request the register file accepted

n_conflict.event: one per read request presented and refused; the request is retried, not lost

n_wait.event: one per CYCLE in which at least one request was refused -- a cycle count, not a request count

n_orphan.event: one per response whose entry was flushed after the read was accepted; absorbed, never written

memory_model.note: tb/common/tnca_mem_model.v -- a testbench model, so these describe the experiment rather than the design

n_stall_cycles.event: one per cycle a request was held off

n_reorder.event: one per response returned out of request order

n_multi_eligible.event: one per cycle with more than one response eligible

n_multi_complete.event: one per cycle in which more than one barrier completed

sampling.rule: COUNT-05: counting is unconditional and has no enable. There is no configuration in which the numbers change, because there is no configuration -- which is a stronger guarantee than 'disabling sampling does not perturb results' and is why no disable exists.
sampling.storage: no counter is software-addressable memory; they are read through the device's response fields, so enabling them adds no software-visible storage
